Phase 4 Business Case · Pattern Setter

One canonical Phase 4 surface that applies to all five Moves (Move 0 Kyriba de-risk, Move 1 AI on top, Move 2 vendor consolidation, Move 3 federated IT, Move 4 federated risk). Worked example: Move 1 · Morgan Street · four AI capabilities post-Kyriba. CFO Sarah Lindqvist is the primary reader.

Companion to 02-demo-spine-architecture.html §5 (Move 1 lifecycle) and 01-lakeshore-federated-structure-brief.md (Morgan Street CXO bench, Kyriba status, finserv benchmarks). Visual + fidelity bar for Wave 3 spec L12.

Projected Modeled · pre-mobilization Realized Actuals from Move 5 mobilization tracking H High confidence (corpus-cited + rate-card bound) M Medium (benchmark-anchored but estimated) L Low (assumption-heavy)

Section 1 · What makes a CFO-grade business case

The pattern this page sets is the antithesis of a deck with hopeful numbers. A CFO-grade business case is a model the CFO can stress-test, edit, sign, and defend in front of an audit committee. Five locked rules from the package README apply here:

1 · No claim without provenance

Every dollar on this page traces to either (a) a rate card line item, (b) the estimation engine’s P50/P80/P95 envelope on a specific scope, (c) a Lakefront-realized benchmark from the operating sibling HoldCo, or (d) a finserv knowledge file with the page/range cited. Hover any number to see the chain. If a chain doesn’t resolve, the cell renders as needs-input, not as a plausible-sounding guess.

2 · Foundation-before-AI made financial

Move 1’s business case can only show realized benefits for AI capabilities whose Move 0 dependency gates are green. Capability lines render projected until the gate clears, then transition to realized as Move 5 mobilization posts actuals. The page literally refuses to model a $ benefit for Cap 1 (12-week forecast) while G4 (historical position reconstruction) is red.

3 · No fake completion

Realized figures only exist once Move 5 tracking has actuals to point at. Until then, the realized column is dashes. There is no aspirational state and no “assumed to be tracking to plan” bleed-through. Projected and realized are visually distinct (purple-dashed vs green-solid) so an audit committee can never confuse them.

4 · HoldCo sovereignty in the numbers

Morgan Street’s business case shows Morgan Street’s numbers. Lakefront’s realized comparables are cited as benchmark evidence but never co-mingled into Morgan Street’s totals. L0 sees the headline NPV and approval status; L0 does not see Morgan Street’s raw rate-card line items unless granted. The holding_group_id substrate enforces this.

5 · No demo-only assumption

Every assumption (forecast accuracy lift, fraud detection precision, working capital unlock %, FTE redeployment rate) is either anchored in Lakefront-realized data, in a finserv knowledge file with citation, or in a corpus pattern with a confidence rating. The assumption panel lets the CFO override any of these with their own number, but the default cannot be a made-up figure.

What this page is not

Not a forecast tool. Not an FP&A model. Not a procurement RFP scorecard (Source handles that). It is a decision-grade business case: NPV + payback + sensitivities + provenance, sized for an audit committee to approve once and revisit each phase gate.

Honest answer: you’re right to push on this. The 85% default sits between two anchors:

Confidence L: the 18% probability is from a cohort, not Morgan Street-specific; no Lakefront comparable. Surface tags as L; CFO routinely overrides to 8-12% in their sign-off snapshot. Page records the override and the rationale.

Well-formed provenance means: every step has a named source, every step is a hop the audit cmte can follow, and the engine can recompute end-to-end if any node is edited. Mal-formed provenance (a $ figure with no chain, or a step labelled “industry standard” with no citation) is refused at write time; the cell renders as needs-input and is flagged in the export.

Section 5 · P50 / P80 / P95 bands — what they mean financially

The estimation engine emits three points per line item, not a single point. They are calibrated against Lakefront-realized + finserv corpus + modernization pattern pack benchmarks.

P50 · modal estimate

The most likely outcome. 50% probability of overrun, 50% of under. Use this for the headline number when presenting to IC. Treat as the operating plan target.

P80 · commit-plan estimate

80% confidence the true cost will be at or below this. Use this for budget commits and cash reserves. Most CFOs sign cash commitments to P80.

P95 · risk-reserve estimate

95% confidence ceiling. Use this for audit cmte tail-risk discussion and for setting risk reserves. Crossing P95 is the trigger to re-baseline the case.

How the engine produces the bands

  1. Base effort from scope decomposition (artifact contracts §3 estimation engine).
  2. Comparable lookup against Lakefront-realized (where available) and finserv corpus patterns. Comparables tighten the variance interval.
  3. Risk multipliers for unknowns: data plane maturity, SME availability, SI familiarity, integration novelty. Each multiplies P80 and P95 independently of P50.
  4. Modernization pattern pack contingency applied at P80 (15%) and P95 (30%) as the residual.

How the CFO reads them

A wide band (P50 vs P95 > 2.5x) means assumption-heavy — expect to revisit at the next phase gate. A tight band (P50 vs P95 < 1.5x) means well-anchored (typically by Lakefront-realized comparables). Sarah Lindqvist’s default posture for Move 1: sign to P50 on benefits, commit to P80 on investment, hold P95 in reserve, re-baseline at Move 5 mid-mobilization checkpoint.

What the snapshot captures

  • Every assumption value (baseline or overridden), with the source citation if baseline and the CFO rationale string if overridden
  • Every line item P50/P80/P95 at sign-off time
  • Every linked rate card version (rate cards are immutable per version)
  • Provenance chain hashes — if a source document changes after sign-off, the chain shows a delta on next view
  • Headline NPV/payback/headline investment

Re-run after sign-off

When Phase 5 mobilization lands actuals or scope shifts, the CFO can re-run the case. The new snapshot shows: this is what changed from your signed baseline · here is the new headline · here is the diff per assumption · do you want to re-sign the baseline or annotate the variance? The approval chain handles re-routing automatically; if scope crosses a threshold (e.g., investment moves from <$5M to >$5M), L0 sponsor approval is added to the chain.

The “no export of nothing” gating

Each export checks artifact completeness before generating. A DOCX board pack with a missing capability narrative or unresolved provenance chain refuses to export and surfaces what to fix. This prevents the failure mode of exporting a polished-looking deck that hides red cells inside. Pattern inherited from the Source module’s export discipline.

Section 8 · How this template flexes per Move

The page composition (headline strip · investment + benefits side-by-side · editable assumptions · sensitivity · Sentinel rail · approval · export) is one template. The line items, assumption defaults, and benefit categories parameterize per Move. Below: how each Move’s Phase 4 instance differs.

Move 0 · Kyriba De-risk

Investment = per-gate remediation across G1-G6. Build = banking H2H integration ($/bank × 10), ERP feed audit (per-source engineer days), entity registry load (legal + tax SME hrs), historical position reconstruction (analyst-weeks), adoption sprint (change lead-weeks), IC auto-recon (built once, becomes Cap 4 in Move 1 — rolled forward as enabler not double-counted).
Benefits = close acceleration ($/day × analyst loaded cost × closes/yr), WC unlock (buffer reduction once positions are clean), fraud avoidance baseline (pre-AI), covenant breach avoidance baseline. Realized benefits start as Wave 1 banks go H2H and ERP variance closes; the realized column fills in chronologically per gate.

Confidence posture: Move 0 is high-confidence on investment (rate cards bound), medium on benefits (benchmark-anchored to Lakefront mature deployment). NPV/payback typically tighter band than Move 1 because no AI model risk.

Move 1 · AI on top of Kyriba (worked example above)

Investment = build (4 capabilities) + run (lakehouse + monitoring + MLOps FTE) + change (training, comms, adoption per capability). Contingency 15%/30% at P80/P95.
Benefits = Cap 1 WC unlock + DSO; Cap 2 BEC fraud avoidance + FTE redeploy; Cap 3 covenant breach avoidance; Cap 4 close acceleration + controller FTE redeploy + cross-Move uplift to Move 2.

Move 2 · Cross-HoldCo vendor consolidation

Investment = sourcing program cost (procurement-led; Source events L-S02/S03/S04/S05 cost-to-execute aggregated), transition cost per consolidation (legal MSA work, contract notifications, transition SI fees if any), change management for switching HoldCos to consolidated agreement.
Benefits = consolidated-rate negotiated discount × renewal-date-weighted (multi-year horizon means some savings don’t hit until contract turn), category-by-category. Per-category benefits cited to 01 structure brief table (Microsoft EA $1.0-1.4M, Workday $0.6-0.9M, etc.) plus finserv file 13 + 20 benchmarks.

Distinguishing features vs Move 1: confidence on benefit side often higher than Move 1 (vendor concessions are well-benchmarked); confidence on investment side often lower (sourcing program effort variable). Approver = L0 OP-Finance Devon Sterling; HoldCo CFOs consulted not signing.

Move 3 · Federated IT strategy + AI marketplace

Investment = federated rollout cost (one shared SI engagement vs three solo); shared architecture standardization (Lakefront landing zone fork-and-customize for 2 HoldCos); federated AI governance setup; marketplace operating cost.
Benefits = implementation cost compression (Gartner-cited 20-30% per platform); ongoing license consolidation (rolls into Move 2 if vendor-overlapping); accelerated AI capability deployment (Lakefront’s 3 production workloads forked to siblings — saves 60-80% of POC cost per).

Per-HoldCo benefit attribution is touchier here; the model surfaces per-HoldCo allocation as an editable assumption (default: equal split or proportional-to-revenue). L0 OP-Tech Marcus Rhee approves; HoldCo CIOs consulted.

Move 4 · Federated risk + governance

Investment = federated risk dashboard build + ongoing operating cadence (quarterly review SME time + L0 CCO time + HoldCo GC time); concentration mitigation actions (e.g., splitting cyber carriers = legal + broker fees).
Benefits = expected-loss reduction on concentration risks (cyber carrier failure · audit firm conflict · banking single-counterparty), probability-weighted; compliance audit cost reduction (federated approach saves repeated audit prep across HoldCos); avoided regulatory penalty (probability-weighted).

Almost all benefits low-confidence (assumption-heavy) here. Move 4 case is presented more as risk-reduction insurance than as NPV-positive. Headline often shows NPV barely positive but tail-risk reduction substantial; CFO and L0 sponsor read both columns together.

Provenance stepbusiness_case_evidencePer line, ordered, with source-type enum (rate_card, engine, corpus, loaded_doc, lakefront_realized, assumption_override)
Rate cardrate_card · rate_card_versionVersioned; lines reference a specific version; sign-off pins the version
Assumptionbusiness_case_assumptionKey, default value, source citation, current value, CFO override rationale (nullable)
Snapshotbusiness_case_snapshotImmutable; captures all line P50/P80/P95 + all assumption values + headline; created on every sign-off + on demand
Approval signaturebusiness_case_signatureApprover, role, snapshot_id, signed_at; chained per role required
Realized actualbusiness_case_realizedPopulated by Move 5 mobilization; per line per period; pinned to snapshot baseline

Open implementation questions for Codex

  • NPV recompute live-edit budget: target sub-300ms for 12-row recompute; if engine round-trip exceeds, ship with client-side cache of base coefficients + server confirm.
  • Provenance hash strategy: SHA-256 of normalized source content; on view, re-hash source and flag if drifted (rate card version change, loaded doc replaced, corpus pattern updated).
  • Audit cmte chair role mapping: does Morgan Street audit cmte chair have an AbarVa identity, or is sign-off email-only with countersigned PDF? L02 loader spec needs the answer.
  • Cross-Move attribution (e.g., Cap 4 uplift to Move 2): currently modelled as a single-line conservative attribution; longer-term move to a proper attribution model with named factors.

End of pattern setter. This page is the visual + fidelity bar for Wave 3 spec L12. Per-Move Phase 4 instances (Move 0 L05 · Move 1 L09 · Move 2 L06 · Move 3 L10 · Move 4 L11) consume this template via parameterization. Companion: 10-mobilization-pattern-setter.html — Phase 5 takes the signed snapshot from this page and operationalizes it into 30/60/90 with realized-actual feedback into this surface.
